planning_note: Organize the module into dual‑clock domain code regions: write‑side nibble accumulation and RAM write, read‑side RAM read and address update, pointer synchronization and flag generation, and output logic.

structural_blocks.purpose: Declare FIFO depth/address parameters, RAM storage, pointer registers, nibble accumulation registers, and byte‑enable register.
must_appear: adr_i, adr_o, tmp, we, ft registers

structural_blocks.purpose: On wclk rising edge, accumulate 4‑bit data into tmp, shift byte‑write enables, and when a full word is ready write to ram[adr_i] and increment adr_i.
On rclk rising edge, update read pointer adr_o when a valid read occurs; keep read data available on q (combinational or registered) and ensure empty‑condition hold.
structural_blocks.code_shape: clocked sequential region (rclk) with optional direct output assignment

structural_blocks.purpose: Generate full, empty, and mem_empt flags by synchronizing and comparing write‑side and read‑side pointers. Must safely cross clock domains.
structural_blocks.code_shape: mixed sequential (synchroniser registers) and combinational comparison

structural_blocks.purpose: (Optional) If the preceding read‑domain block does not directly drive q and mem_empt, provide a dedicated combinational block that extracts these outputs from ram and pointer state.
must_appear: none (can be merged into other blocks)

semantic_modes.meaning: independent write‑side nibble accumulation and read‑side word retrieval

state_model.notes: read pointer; increments after a read while not empty; wraps with high‑bit toggle; after reset points to RAM location that will be output on subsequent reads when empty

global_invariants: Write operation only updates state when wr is active.
Read operation only alters read pointer when rd is active and FIFO not empty.
Full/empty flags must be stable and glitch‑free in the consuming domains.
mem_empt reflects available space in words, not nibbles.
open_semantic_questions: Whether q output is registered or purely combinational.
Exact byte‑packing order of nibbles into tmp (spec only says “accumulated”, not nibble‑position mapping).
Preferred synchronisation method (2‑stage DFF or Gray‑code pointer) is not specified.

responsibilities: Provide parameter constants and all state‑holding declarations.
timing_semantics: Asynchronous reset (rst) clears all registers declared here.
touched_objects: ram, adr_i, adr_o, we, tmp, ft, and any pointer‑width extension bits
coupling_rules: All other blocks depend on these declarations; no write‑domain block may modify rclk‑side registers, and vice‑versa, except through synchronised paths in B4.
forbidden_drift: Do not create additional asynchronous storage or un‑clocked registers.

responsibilities: Implement nibble accumulation, byte‑enable shifting, RAM write, and write‑pointer management.
timing_semantics: Fully synchronous to wclk; outputs to RAM (ram[adr_i]) and pointer updates are registered.
The RAM write occurs on the rising edge when a full word is ready; data must be committed to RAM before the pointer increments.
coupling_rules: Must respect we reset value (8’h1) and wrap‑around pointer behaviour.
Must signal word‑ready to read side only through the synchronised pointer in B4.
forbidden_drift: Do not presume the width of the wrap‑around extension bit beyond what is necessary for full/empty distinction.
Do not add speculative writes without wr.

responsibilities: Update read pointer when rd is active and FIFO not empty; provide q output.
timing_semantics: adr_o update on rclk rising edge; q may be combinational from ram[adr_o] or registered. If registered, care must be taken to meet external read‑data hold timing.
touched_objects: adr_o, q (if assigned here), ram (read access)
coupling_rules: Must not update adr_o when empty signal (from B4) is asserted.
When empty, must hold the data from the last valid read address on q (as per spec empty behaviour).
forbidden_drift: Do not produce q from any source other than ram[adr_o] (or a registered version of it).
Do not assume rd handshake extends beyond the current clock cycle.

responsibilities: Safely synchronise write‑ and read‑side pointers, generate full, empty, and mem_empt.
timing_semantics: Synchroniser chains run on their respective clocks; flag outputs are potentially delayed by 2–3 clock cycles, which is inherent to asynchronous FIFO design.
Flag combinational logic produces glitch‑free outputs only after synchronisers have settled.
touched_objects: full, empty, mem_empt outputs; internal synchronised versions of adr_i, adr_o
coupling_rules: Must use the same pointer width and wrap‑around extension as declared in B1.
Empty/full determination uses the high‑bit comparison technique implied by the spec wrap‑around test.
mem_empt computes available words (e.g., pointer difference masked to FIFO depth).
forbidden_drift: Do not infer handshake signals or additional control paths beyond the static flags.
Do not bypass synchroniser stages except when explicitly justified by a known safe user constraint.

responsibilities: If q or mem_empt are not directly driven in their originating blocks, provide terminal combinational assignments from the synchronised state.
timing_semantics: Purely combinational; timing is determined by input arrival from upstream blocks.
touched_objects: q, mem_empt (may also set them in B3/B4)
coupling_rules: Outputs must match the behaviour specified in the interface contract.
forbidden_drift: Do not introduce new logic that changes the meaning of mem_empt (only 2‑bit word space).

chosen_decisions.decision: Split the module into five blocks: parameter/register declaration, write‑domain sequencer, read‑domain sequencer, flag synchronisation, and optional output‑only block. Aligns with spec’s explicit dual‑clock FIFO structure and pointer comparison requirements.
chosen_decisions.reason: Separate clock domains and cross‑clock logic are the main complexity; this decomposition keeps retrieval and future code merge manageable while honouring every spec line.

deferred_decisions: Exact byte‑packing order of nibbles into tmp (which bit position for which nibble) – deferred until local generation; will use a straightforward right‑to‑left accumulation unless later spec clarification forces otherwise.
Whether to register q output – deferred to timing closure requirements; skeleton allows both.
Use of Gray‑coded pointers versus 2‑stage DFF synchronisers for pointer crossing – deferred; both satisfy "high‑bit flips" test but have different area/latency trade‑offs.
structural_risks: B4 (flag synchronisation) concentrates all cross‑clock logic and may become a maintenance burden if future specs add more flags.
B2 and B3 are tightly coupled to B1 register widths; parameter changes must be reflected in all pointer logic.
behavioral_risks: If q is not registered, the read output may glitch when adr_o changes; consuming logic must guarantee rd/empty handshake to avoid capturing invalid data.
Cross‑clock path latency may cause full/empty to lag; host must tolerate conservative flag timing (inherent in asynchronous FIFO).
